changes: Experimental fix for a timed lap not restarting after restoring a checkpoint before the finish line.
Captures the native sector progression gate with F6 and restores it with the car on F7. Lap times and records are not rewound.
Keeps the interrupted attempt untimed while allowing LMU to recognize the next sector or finish-line crossing.
Restart LMU to load the v26 module and create a new checkpoint. In-game verification of this fix is pending.
Experimental lap-scoring change, pending automated and in-game verification.
F7 removes timing eligibility from a counted attempt while preserving finish-line counting and existing next-lap restrictions. Native no-count states remain unchanged.
F6 remains capture-only. The reported first-lap timing failure after saving at Le Mans still needs in-game confirmation.
Restart LMU after upgrading to load the v25 reset module.
Moves Open LMU without EAC to Active Reset and explains offline launch in Guide.
Shows an explicit EAC warning and disables Save/Restore and their shortcuts, including when Windows hides the protected game path.
Monitors for late EAC detection and stops the reset listener cooperatively while overlays remain available.
Experimental release. Bugs remain possible and further fixes are planned.
Fixes error 92004 when LMU publishes a stable bodywork model with zero deformable components. Models with components retain full bodywork restoration.
Verifies fuel consumption and tyre wear enabled or disabled without requiring their values to change. Session settings are preserved.
Keeps loading, model changes, damaged checkpoints and invalid memory guarded. Restart LMU after upgrading to the v24 reset module.
Experimental diagnostic release. Known and undiscovered bugs remain; further fixes are expected.
Adds Help > Export diagnostics to save bounded text logs, system graphics information and session context without uploading anything.
Identifies the exact bodywork layout check behind error 92004, with component, mesh and observed limits. This release diagnoses the refusal; it does not fix unsupported bodywork layouts.
Requires an LMU restart when upgrading to the v23 diagnostic reset module.
Keeps first-launch setup open until a valid LMU folder is confirmed, with a native Windows folder picker.
Separates public SDK overlays from Active Reset so protected game discovery and online sessions do not require the reset listener.
Prevents the reset listener from starting with EAC or without confirmed offline Practice context. Live online overlay verification is pending.
Matches overlay updates to the selected display refresh rate, including fractional rates and monitor changes.
Hides widgets promptly when LMU pauses, with faster detection when telemetry stops advancing.
Keeps widgets visible through F7 instead of briefly hiding them while reset histories are cleared.
Updates overlay telemetry at 60 Hz and presents the latest frame in sync with the display.
Updates Leaderboard and Relative gaps between scoring samples using measured vehicle movement. Estimated gaps are marked with ~.
Confirms visible front bodywork repair in the Mercedes-AMG LMGT3 live test with the v22 reset module.
Fixes a false damaged-car warning when saving a healthy car or a car repaired in the pits.
Keeps the bodywork checks for damage events, severity and original vertex data. A render flag alone no longer rejects the checkpoint.
Visible bodywork restoration still requires a successful live save and impact test.
Adds experimental bodywork restoration to Active Reset for supported CPU graphics buffers. Live validation is still pending.
Coordinates bodywork updates with physical reset and restores previous graphics state if contact rebuilding fails.
Explains when bodywork is busy or a rebuilt vehicle requires a new checkpoint.
Renames active reset source files and updates build scripts for easier maintenance.
Wait for LMU to leave pause before connecting Active Reset, even when the player still controls the car.
Includes the aerodynamic recovery from 0.2.7; live validation and visible bodywork repair remain pending.
Active Reset now includes impact-altered aerodynamic coefficients and their dependent calculations.
Aerodynamic recovery has passed local transaction and rollback tests; the new module still requires validation in LMU.
Visible bodywork deformation, punctures and detached parts remain outside the supported restore.
Save and restore both suspension hinge reference axes, including the axis changed by an impact.
Validate suspension alignment state and restore its previous values if the transaction fails.
Post-impact stability still needs a live test. Front bodywork, punctures and detached assemblies are not repaired.
Experimental suspension deformation recovery. The live impact test exposed a crash; front bodywork repair remains incomplete.
Validate bent-wheel rotation and angular velocity instead of rejecting every impact damage flag.
Show a specific refusal for a detached wheel; rebuilding detached suspension is not supported yet.
Removed Brake lock from the widget list, settings, previews and saved layouts.
Keep recognized manufacturer logos through temporary opponent telemetry gaps while clearing them when the car or session changes.
Show a notice when another Sector instance is already running, so launching a newer executable does not silently reopen an older background version.
Fixed reset reconnection after updating Sector while LMU retains a stopped module from an earlier release.
Recognize reset hosts v16 and v17 during reconnection, with DLL integrity, stopped-state and restored-hook verification.
Leaderboard and Relative logos now identify each car from its telemetry model and vehicle file, including team-only scoring names.
Fixed resets rejected by a field count belonging to a different car. Native preflight now validates each complete vehicle plan.
Brake lock now shows a learned pedal limit below the warning threshold, adjusted for wheel slip and comparable steering, speed and load conditions.
The brake limit stays independent of the current pedal and identifies the limiting wheel.
Prevent telemetry updates from repositioning widgets during layout dragging.
Brake-lock warnings now account for combined longitudinal slip and slip angle.
Restore the saved failure state after an impact when the vehicle assembly remains intact.
Updated widget opacity defaults and fixed class badges and vehicle logo matching.
Save and restore checkpoints directly from Home. Edit shortcuts in Active Reset.
Overlay toggles no longer disable unrelated Home buttons.
Added this version history under Help > Changelog.
Removed Sample labels from overlay previews and layout handles.
Simplified the idle connection footer.
Added the Sector launch animation with animated lettering.
The animation plays only at startup and supports skipping and reduced motion.
Deployment maps follow the selected LMH or LMDh vehicle.
Removed the deployment-step rectangles from the Hybrid widget.
Added the Hybrid widget with battery, electric power and map recommendations.
Updated the leaderboard with tyre compounds and virtual energy; player rows stay inside their class.
Added brake-lock forecasting and kept all four tyres visible.
Added Brake lock, Tyres and Stint planner widgets with telemetry and estimated flat spots.
Added Home with session details, checkpoint status, overlay controls and an LMU launcher.
Refined overlay switches, display selection and layout controls.
Widget resizing now updates continuously while dragging.
Updated documentation, licensing and app screenshots.
Animated first-run setup and guided-tour popups.
Added first-run setup with automatic LMU folder detection and manual selection.
Added an optional introductory guide after setup.
Added Edit > Settings.
Aligned the Active Reset and Overlay tabs with equal sizing and spacing.
Added the Help menu with access to Guide.
Connected overlay widgets to game telemetry and expanded column customization.
Refined layout sizing, transparent logos, window controls and the close dialog.
First portable Sector desktop release for Windows.
Active Reset shortcuts, customizable telemetry overlays, settings, guide and background operation.
